claims.text: Resistance to combined wear and corrosion in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is governed by retention of its fine L12/B2 lamellar dual-phase microstructure.
Homogeneous Cr availability enables rapid repassivation in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Structural stability in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 sustains a stable, low-shear tribo-layer near 50 °C.
DS2205 undergoes phase redistribution that compromises passivation and increases wear and corrosion.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has an approximately 71% L12 and 29% B2 lamellar microstructure.
Hot-rolled DS2205 has approximately 52% austenite and 48% ferrite.
Temperature controls the competition between sliding-induced depassivation and thermally activated repassivation.
Near 50 °C, rapid passive-film repair and a stable polishing tribo-layer minimize wear and corrosion in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
At 25 °C, insufficient repassivation increases abrasion and debris-assisted degradation.
At 100 °C, fragile oxide layers repeatedly rupture and increase abrasion and debris-assisted degradation.
DS2205 experiences an undesirable austenite-to-ferrite phase redistribution that destabilizes its passive film.
Relative to DS2205, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will exhibit a smaller wear volume under matched test conditions.
Relative to DS2205, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will exhibit a lower coefficient of friction under matched test conditions.
Relative to DS2205, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will exhibit a substantially lower tribo-corrosion wear rate, especially near 50 °C.
Both alloys may exhibit increased wear and corrosion at 25 °C and 100 °C relative to 50 °C.
At 25 °C and 100 °C, DS2205 will degrade more than AlCoCrFeNi2.1 because of less stable passivation and debris-driven wear.
The proposed predictions are scoped to short-term testing at 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, 3–9 Hz, and a 3.5 mm stroke with an alumina counter-body in deionized water.

contradictions.description: The principal tribo-corrosion comparison is specified in low-ionic-strength deionized water, but potentiodynamic polarization is specified in 3.5 wt.% NaCl. Results from the latter environment would not directly test passivation under the stated primary environment unless it is explicitly designated as a separate ancillary test.
